components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — the outer box
口 (box) — the inner box; the nested shape echoes an old swirl that suggested turning back

example.fact: 回 is the word for going back to where you came from: 回家, 回国, 回来. It is also a measure word for occurrences in speech (去过两回 'been twice'), and it appears in 回答 'to answer' and 回忆 'to recall'.

components.note: Simplified from 當; the modern shape is a shorthand with no readable picture

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎngdà le xiǎng dāng lǎoshī.
example.english: When I grow up I want to be a teacher.
example.fact: 当 means 'to act as': 当老师 'be a teacher', and in 当时 'at that time' it marks a moment. Read as dàng it is 'to treat as': 当真 'take seriously', 上当 'be fooled'. The two readings change the meaning.

components.note: 冂 (frame) — in this simplified form it stands in for the eye 目 of the traditional 見
儿 (legs/person) — the person doing the seeing

example.fact: 见 often follows other verbs as a result: 看见 'catch sight of', 听见 'hear'. 见面 'meet in person' is a verb-object word, so you say 见了面. 再见 'goodbye' literally means 'see again'.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — money was once made of metal coins
戋 (jiān) gives the sound; qián is a close but not exact match

example.fact: 钱 is 'money': 多少钱 'how much', 零钱 'small change', 没钱 'broke'. Chinese counts it with 块 (kuài) in speech: 五块钱. 钱 is also a common surname, pronounced the same.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken exclamation
奥 (ào) gives a rough sound hint

example.fact: 噢 is an interjection of realization, interchangeable with 哦 in most writing. The tone carries the feeling: a falling ò means 'now I get it', and a rising ó shows surprise or doubt. It mostly shows up in informal text and subtitles.

excludeSuggestion: interjection that is a spelling variant of 哦

components.note: 口 (mouth) — eating happens at the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a loose sound hint

example.fact: 你吃了吗？ is a traditional everyday greeting, like 'How are you?' 吃 reaches into idioms: 吃醋 'be jealous', 吃惊 'be startled', 吃苦 'endure hardship'. Medicine is 吃药, 'eaten' not 'drunk'.

components.note: 一 (bar) — the latch or bar across a door
廾 (two hands) — lifting the bar; simplified from 開

example.fact: 开 is a very flexible verb: 开灯 'turn on the light', 开车 'drive', 开会 'hold a meeting', 开始 'begin', 开玩笑 'joke'. Note that 开 'open' also means 'turn on', not just physical openings.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house
豕 (pig) — under the roof; the standard explanation is that pigs were kept in the home, though scholars debate it

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
example.english: There are four people in my family.
example.fact: 家 means 'home' and 'family': 回家 'go home'. It is a suffix for experts (作家 'writer', 科学家 'scientist') and a measure word for businesses (一家店 'a shop'). 大家 means 'everyone'.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken question word
那 (nà) is a close sound match for nǎ

example.fact: 哪 asks 'which' before a measure word: 哪个 'which one', 哪本书. 哪儿 or 哪里 means 'where'. Don't confuse 哪 with 那; the 口 on the left makes it a question. 哪里哪里 is a modest reply to a compliment.

components.note: 彳 (left step) — a foot taking a step
亍 (right step) — the other foot; together they suggest a crossroads or walking

example.fact: 行 is a common 'OK': 行！ 'Sure!', 不行 'won't do'. As háng it means 'row' or 'profession' (银行 'bank', 内行 'expert'). 旅行 'travel' keeps the walking sense.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — an old sense of 前 was 'to cut', with 'front' taking over later

example.english: He is standing in front of me.
example.fact: 前 works for both space and time: 前面 'in front', 以前 'before', 前天 'the day before yesterday', 前年 'the year before last'. For 'former' it is a prefix: 前男友 'ex-boyfriend'.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken greeting
海 (hǎi) is a close sound match for hāi

example.fact: 嗨 is a borrowing of English 'hi', widely used in informal greetings. It is also an older exclamation of regret or realization: 嗨，别提了！ 'Ugh, don't even mention it!' For proper greetings, 你好 is more standard.

components.note: 丬 (bed-plank shape) — the left part, from the older 將
寸 (hand) — the right part; 將 earlier meant to take or lead

example.english: The company will open next year.
example.fact: 将 is a formal 'will/about to', common in news and announcements; speech prefers 要 or 会. 将来 means 'the future'. As jiàng it means 'general': 将军, 大将.

components.note: Simplified from 車, an overhead picture of a cart with two wheels joined by an axle

example.english: I take the car to work.
example.fact: 车 is a general word for any wheeled vehicle: 汽车 'car', 火车 'train', 自行车 'bicycle', 出租车 'taxi'. Its measure word is 辆. In Chinese chess the piece 车 is the 'chariot' (rook).

components.note: 日 (sun) — the passing of time is tied to the sun
寸 (cùn) stands in for the traditional 寺 (sì), the sound part; shí is only a rough match

example.fact: 时候 means 'the time when': …的时候 'when…'. 小时 is 'hour', 时间 'time', and 有时 'sometimes'. The simplified form 时 reshapes the old 時.

components.note: Simplified from 殺; the modern shape is a shorthand, not a readable picture

example.pinyin: Nóngmín shā le yì zhī jī.
example.fact: 杀 is used literally for killing and also figuratively: 杀价 'bargain hard', 杀毒 'run antivirus', 杀菌 'sterilize'.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a vocal sound
厄 (è) gives the sound exactly

example.fact: 呃 is a filler sound that shows hesitation, like 'er' or 'um'. It can also imitate a hiccup. It appears mostly in dialogue and chat messages, and is rare in formal writing.

components.note: A small low table with legs; the 'how many' sense is a borrowing

example.english: How many children do you have?
example.fact: 几 asks about small numbers (typically under ten): 几点 'what time', 几岁 'how old (a child)'. For large or unknown amounts use 多少. It also means 'several': 几天 'a few days'. Read jī, it means 'small table', as in 茶几.

components.note: Simplified form that merged the old 后 'queen' with 後 'after'; learn it as one unit

example.pinyin: Chī fàn hòu wǒ qù sànbù.
example.english: I go for a walk after eating.
example.fact: In simplified Chinese 后 took over for the traditional 後 'after, behind', and the older 后 'queen' (皇后) merged with it. 以后 means 'afterwards', 后面 'behind', 后天 'the day after tomorrow'.

components.note: 匕 (spoon, person) — written twice, two figures standing side by side to be compared

example.fact: The comparison pattern is A 比 B + adjective: 他比我高. Don't add 很 or 非常 after 比; use 更, 还 or an amount: 高三厘米 'three cm taller'. 比 also means 'compete' in 比赛 'match' and 'ratio' in 比例.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) gives a loose sound hint for xiē
二 (two) — a small number, as in 'a couple'

example.fact: 些 almost never stands alone: 一些 'some', 这些 'these', 那些 'those', 有些 'some of'. It works for countable and uncountable nouns: 一些水 'some water'. For a smaller amount, 一点儿 is common.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — asking aloud
门 (mén) gives the sound, a close match for wèn

example.hanzi: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
example.english: May I ask you a question?
example.fact: 问 takes the person asked directly: 问老师 'ask the teacher'. 请问 starts a polite question, 问好 means 'say hello (on behalf of)'. 问题 means both 'question' and 'problem'.

components.note: 走 (walk) — movement upward
己 (jǐ) is a close sound hint for qǐ

example.english: I get up at six every day.
example.fact: 起 works as a verb and a direction ending: 起床 'get up', 站起来 'stand up', 想起来 'remember'. It also forms 一起 'together' and 对不起 'sorry'. 起 counts incidents in speech: 一起事故.

components.note: 户 (door) — the left part, a household or place
斤 (axe) — the right part; its link to the meaning is unclear, so treat the pair as a memory aid

example.fact: 所 is a measure word for institutions (一所大学). It also appears in 所以 'therefore', 所有 'all', and the pattern 因为…所以… 'because…so…'. In formal writing it turns verbs into nouns: 所见 'what one sees'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — someone residing
主 (zhǔ) gives the sound, a close match for zhù

example.fact: 住 is 'to reside' and 'to stay overnight': 住酒店 'stay at a hotel'. As a verb ending it means 'firmly': 记住 'remember', 站住 'halt!', 拿住 'hold on'. 住院 means 'be hospitalised'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the original sense is dividing items among people
牛 (cow) — the traditional explanation is dividing up livestock, offered here as a memory aid

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn yīfu.
example.english: I bought a piece of clothing.
example.fact: 件 counts upper-body clothing (一件衬衫), matters (一件事), and documents or luggage (一件行李). For trousers or skirts the measure word is 条. 件 also appears in 文件 'document' and 邮件 'mail'.

components.note: 一 (line) — a straight line, the target
止 (foot) — a foot stopping or heading straight at it

example.fact: 正在 + verb shows an action in progress. 正 also means 'exactly': 正好 'just right', 正确 'correct'. When it means 'first month', 正月, it is read zhēng.

components.note: Simplified from 並, which showed two people standing side by side; the modern shape is reduced

example.pinyin: Wǒ bìng bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: I really don't know about this matter.
example.fact: 并 before 不 or 没 strengthens a denial: 并不贵 'not expensive at all'. 并且 means 'moreover'. Its basic sense 'side by side' appears in 并排 'side by side' and 合并 'merge'.

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — an action done by hand
方 (fāng) gives the sound, a close match for fàng

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Please put the book on the table.
example.fact: 放 means to place something or to release it: 放心 'rest assured', 放假 'have a holiday', 放学 'school lets out'. It also means 'play (a recording)': 放音乐.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — handling something
高 (gāo) gives a close sound hint

example.fact: 搞 is a colloquial catch-all verb: 搞定 'get it done', 搞错 'get it wrong', 搞笑 'funny'. It can sound slightly informal, even negative (搞鬼 'play tricks'), so it isn't used in formal writing.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a stick is wooden
奉 (fèng) is a loose sound hint

example.fact: 棒 literally means 'stick' (棒球 'baseball'), but in speech it's a casual 'great': 真棒！ 'Awesome!' 你真棒 is a popular praise for children and learners.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a mother
马 (mǎ) gives the sound, a close match

example.fact: 妈 is usually doubled to 妈妈. A classic tone-practice sentence is 妈妈骂马 'Mom scolds the horse' (Māma mà mǎ), which combines 妈, 骂 and 马.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground
也 (yě) is only a distant sound hint

example.english: He is sitting on the ground.
example.fact: 地 dì is 'ground' and 'place': 地方 'place', 地铁 'subway', 土地 'land'. The same character is also the structural particle de that turns adjectives into adverbs: 慢慢地走 'walk slowly'.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement
井 (jǐng) is a close sound match, apart from the tone

example.fact: 进 is 'enter', the opposite of 出. It shows direction after verbs: 走进来 'walk in'. It also means 'to advance': 进步 'progress'. 进口 means both 'entrance' and 'import'.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) — the left part, shaped from an older 辛 (xīn), which provided the sound
斤 (axe) — chopping fresh wood is the traditional picture of something newly made

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge xīn shǒujī.
example.fact: 新 appears in 新年 'New Year', 新闻 'news', 新鲜 'fresh'. Its opposite is 旧. As an adverb it means 'newly': 新来的 'newly arrived'. 新 is also the first part of the country name 新加坡 'Singapore'.

components.note: 你 (you) — the top part
心 (heart) — the heart beneath it, showing respect

example.fact: 您 is the respectful 'you' for elders, customers or strangers. It is singular, so for two people say 您二位 rather than 您们. Using 您 with friends sounds distant or jokingly formal.

components.note: An old form shows a window (口) in a house, an opening that faces outward; the modern shape keeps that outline

example.fact: 向 as a preposition means 'towards': 向前看 'look ahead', 向他道歉 'apologise to him', 向老师学习 'learn from the teacher'. 方向 means 'direction', and 一向 means 'all along'.

components.note: Three horizontal strokes, a direct picture of the number

example.fact: 三 is also written 叁 on contracts and cheques, where the extra strokes make forgery harder. It can mean 'several' in idioms: 三思 'think carefully', 再三 'repeatedly'. 三月 is March.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken particle
麻 (má) gives the sound exactly

example.fact: 嘛 ends a sentence to say 'it's obvious' or to coax: 不会就问嘛 'just ask if you don't know'. It is warmer or more insistent than 吗, and it is toneless here.

components.note: 耂 (old person with long hair) — the upper part
匕 (changed person) — the lower part; together they suggest a person who has aged

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.
example.fact: 老 is respectful in Chinese: 老师 'teacher', 老板 'boss', 老人 'elder'. It also means 'always' (老是迟到 'always late') and prefixes names: 老王. 老 for friends means long-standing, not elderly.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's position
立 (to stand) — the place where one stands

example.fact: 位 is the polite measure word for people: 三位客人 'three guests'. As a noun it means 'position': 座位 'seat', 位置 'location', 学位 'degree'. In restaurants 几位？ is the standard question to guests.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — an action by hand
卓 (zhuó) is a distant sound hint for diào

example.fact: 掉 is 'fall' and also a verb ending of removal: 吃掉 'eat up', 扔掉 'throw away', 丢掉 'lose'. 掉头 means 'turn around' (a vehicle).

components.note: An old form shows a foot (止) ahead of a person (儿), meaning 'going first'

example.fact: 先 is 'first': 先…再… 'first…then…' sequences actions. 先生 literally means 'one born earlier' and is used for 'Mr.', 'teacher' and 'husband'. 先 comes before the verb.

components.note: An old form shows a foot stepping out from a line, meaning 'to go'; the 'of' sense is borrowed

example.pinyin: Chī fàn zhīqián qǐng xǐ shǒu.
example.english: Please wash your hands before eating.
example.fact: 之 is the classical 'of' (的) that survives in set phrases: 之前 'before', 之后 'after', 之间 'between'. Fractions use it: 三分之一 'one third', 百分之十 'ten percent'.

components.note: Simplified from 買, which showed a net (网) over a shell (贝), i.e., catching goods; the modern shape is reduced

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì bēi kāfēi.
example.english: I'd like to buy a coffee.
example.fact: 买 (mǎi) and 卖 (mài) look alike; 卖 has an extra 十 on top, and a handy rule is that 'selling' has more on top. Together they make 买卖 'business'. 买单 is 'ask for the bill', a common phrase in restaurants.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — seeds and crops
中 (zhōng) gives the sound, a close match for zhǒng

example.english: This kind of fruit is very sweet.
example.fact: 种 zhǒng is 'kind' as a measure word (这种, 各种 'all kinds') and 'seed'. Read zhòng it means 'to plant': 种花 'grow flowers'. The tones separate the two uses.

components.note: A drawing of a hand with the fingers spread

example.fact: 手 forms 手机 'mobile phone' (literally 'hand machine') and marks skilled people: 歌手 'singer', 选手 'athlete'. It is the base of the 扌 radical on many action verbs.

components.note: 从 (two people) — two figures sitting
土 (earth) — sitting on the ground

example.fact: 坐 is also 'ride/take' for transport you sit inside: 坐地铁, 坐飞机. For bikes you 'straddle' (骑), and for driving you use 开. 请坐 is the polite 'please sit down'.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — drinking
曷 (hé) gives the sound, a close match for hē

example.english: What would you like to drink?
example.fact: 喝 covers drinks and soup: 喝汤 'have soup' (literally 'drink soup'). Medicine is usually 吃药 but Chinese medicine soup is 喝. In 喝彩 'cheer', the same character is read hè.

components.note: Simplified from 與; the modern shape is reduced to a few strokes

example.pinyin: Tā yǔ péngyou yìqǐ qù lǚxíng.
example.fact: 与 is a more formal 'and/with' than 和, common in titles and writing: 战争与和平 'War and Peace'. It also appears in 参与 'participate' and 与其…不如… 'rather than…'.
